One editor (E387), one article, never put back, so not level 3.

items.label: contested
items.description: Adds two sentences: the Finnish government still holds to the separate-war view although Finnish officers 'in reality' helped plan Barbarossa, and foreign research agrees Finland was Germany's ally.
items.why: Level 2. Claim on the topic's core question: 'Suomen hallitus pitää edelleen kiinni näkemystä erillissodasta, vaikka todellisuudessa joukko korkea-arvoisia suomalaisupseereita osallistui operaatio Barbarossan suunnitteluun' ('the Finnish government still holds to the separate-war view, although in reality a group of high-ranking Finnish officers took part in planning Operation Barbarossa') and 'Ulkomaisessa historiantutkimuksessa on kuitenkin vallinnut yhteisymmärrys siitä, että Suomi oli Saksan liittolainen' ('foreign historical research has agreed that Finland was Germany's ally'). items.label: campaign
items.description: Adds paragraphs, cited to one magazine article, saying the Sámi are not more indigenous than the Finns, that prehistoric people cannot be divided into Sámi and Finns, that Sámi identity is under 100 years old and that 'Sápmi' was invented in the 1980s.
items.why: Level 3. Claim (quoted from the added text): 'Saamelaiset eivät ole alkuperäisempiä kuin suomalaiset, vaikka heitä kutsutaan alkuperäiskansaksi' ('The Sámi are not more indigenous than the Finns, although they are called an indigenous people'), 'Suomalaiset ja saamelaiset ovat siis samassa määrin alkuperäisiä kansoja' ('Finns and Sámi are thus equally indigenous peoples'), 'Esihistoriallisia asukkaita ei voi jakaa saamelaisiin ja suomalaisiin' ('prehistoric inhabitants cannot be divided into Sámi and Finns'), 'Saamelaisidentiteetti on alle sata vuotta vanha' ('Sámi identity is under a hundred years old'), '"Saamenmaa" keksittiin 1980-luvulla' ('"Sápmi" was invented in the 1980s'), all cited to one Suomen Kuvalehti article. Community dispute: put back 3 times after removals (16920192 on Saamelaiset two days after the first removal; 17123375 and 17123380 three months later by a second account), and the second removal on Saamelaisten historia (17123675) gives a sourcing reason: 'ei kirjoiteta artikkelia uusiksi yhden lehtijutun perusteella' ('an article is not rewritten on the basis of one magazine article'). Level-3 signals, 3 of 4: articles (added to Saamelaisten historia and Saamelaiset 13 s apart by E173), accounts (two named accounts added it: E173, then E182 put it back with 'Palautettiin lähteistetty teksti' / 'Ihan hyvin näyttää olevan lähteistetty' = 'restored sourced text' / 'seems to be sourced quite well'), persistence (put back 3 times, first insertion 2017-11-23, last 2018-03-02, 99 days apart). Removals: on Saamelaiset rejected after 3 min (16917081) and 3.5 h (16920612), and removed after 4.1 h (17123933, 'palautettu mistä? pesuveden mukana meni paljon artikkeliin tehtyä pikkuhuoltoa' = 'restored from where? a lot of small maintenance went out with the bathwater'); on Saamelaisten historia removed after 8.6 days (16935955, 'Ei kuitenkaan näin' = 'not like this, though') and after 87 min (17123675). Not in the latest revision. The first insertion also tagged existing citations ({{Parempi lähde|kuin saamelaispoliitikon kirja}} = 'better source needed: than a Sámi politician's book'); not counted as source manipulation because no citation was removed or replaced. Candidates c01, c13 (Saamelaisten historia), c17, c06, c07 (Saamelaiset); c28 is the 17123380 re-insertion seen from the other side.
items.notes: c28's removal (17123380) restored a 2017 revision wholesale, so it also took out an anonymous editor's population update (17100871) and other maintenance; E178's 17123933 restored those 4 h later. No separate item for that collateral removal.

items.label: contested
items.description: Turns the redirect 'Metsäsaamelaiset' into an article stating that the Forest Sámi are one of the (four) Sámi groups living in Finland and were refused the Sámi Parliament electoral roll because they lost their language.
items.why: Level 3. Claim: the article text states a disputed group status as fact: 'Metsäsaamelaiset ovat yksi neljästä Suomen alueella elävästä saamelaisryhmästä' ('The Forest Sámi are one of the four Sámi groups living in Finland') and 'Koska metsäsaamelaiset ovat menettäneet kielensä, heitä ei ole hyväksytty Saamelaiskäräjien vaaliluetteloon' ('Because the Forest Sámi have lost their language, they have not been accepted onto the Sámi Parliament's electoral roll'); first summary 'Poistettu ohjaus, koska tämä kansa on olemassa' ('Removed the redirect because this people exists'). (The current article attributes it instead: 'kokevat olevansa' = 'feel that they are'.) Community dispute: removed 4 times by 4 other accounts, twice with sourcing reasons ('lähteetöntä, pysyköön ohjauksena' = 'unsourced, let it stay a redirect', 20025656; 'takaisin ohjaukseksi: lähteetöntä omaa tutkimusta' = 'back to a redirect: unsourced original research', 20029336); {{Lähde}} (citation needed) tags added by another account in the same episode (20025690); a back-and-forth inside the first run (another account replaced the text as 'historiallisesti paikkaansapitävään ja totuudenmukaiseen kuvaukseen' = 'a historically accurate and truthful description', and E233 restored it with 'Sivu oli muokattu paikkansapitämättömäksi' = 'the page had been edited to be inaccurate'); put back 3 times after removals. Level-3 signals, 2 of 4: accounts (two named accounts added the text: E233 created it and put it back once, E235 put it back twice, the second time with references) and persistence (put back 3 times: 20025223, 20025687, 20036982; first insertion 2021-09-28 18:08 UTC, last 2021-10-05 19:00 UTC = 7 days 51 min). One article, no source manipulation. Last removal 20081057 after 23.1 days: 'Takaisin ohjaussivuksi. Tällä hetkellä pelkkä tiivistetty versio sivusta Keminsaamelaiset' ('back to a redirect; at the moment just a condensed version of Keminsaamelaiset'). Inserting revs exclude other accounts' edits swept up by the removals (E296/E297 rewrites, small tweaks by E235/E297/E298/E233 inside c16, E234's redirect-line removal, E100's tags, E76's category). Candidates c08, c16, c15, c02.
items.notes: Labellers disagree: labeller campaign; claude:blind contested (Level 2: a redirect page for Metsäsaamelaiset was repeatedly turned into an article saying the group 'has lost its language, so it has not been accepted to the Sámi Parliament electoral roll' and was turned back as 'unsourced, remain a redirect' and 'unsourced own research'. Several rounds of putting back over about a week, {{Lähde}} templates added, edit summaries from two editors disagreeing over what is accurate. Several named accounts took part but they did not all add the same text, and the dispute looks like a redirect-versus-article fight, so kept below Level 3.). Lowest level kept until a human decides.

items.description: Rewrites the etymology of 'kuningas' so the Germanic-loan origin is only 'claimed', argues the word was used in Finland before Germanic influence, and alters the wording of a quoted source.
items.why: Level 2. Claim: the edit says 'kuningas' is only 'väitetään periytyneen' ('claimed to derive') from Proto-Germanic, adds 'Kantagermaaninen kieli on kuitenkin rekonstruktio ja hypoteesi ... teorian paikkansapitävyyttä ja lainautumisen suuntaa voi vain arvella' ('Proto-Germanic is however a reconstruction and a hypothesis ... the validity of the theory and the direction of borrowing can only be guessed') and 'joten loogisesti sana kuningas tai vastaava on ollut käytössä Suomessakin jo ennen germaanisen kulttuurin vaikutteita' ('so logically the word king or similar was in use in Finland before Germanic influence'). Alongside it, it removed the sentence that Porthan was right that the words are Germanic loans, removed a sentence cited to Vahtola, and changed the wording of the Vahtola quotation inside the reference ('Suomen kuninkaissa oli nähtävästi kyse' -> 'Suomenkin kuninkaissa on voinut olla kyse', 'was apparently' -> 'may have been'). Community dispute: rolled back after 4.2 h (13315992), put back once 42 days later (13407096, summary: 'pitää sanoa "väitetään perityneen kantagermaanista"' = 'it must say "claimed to derive from Proto-Germanic"'), then removed after 6.9 days with 'rv, uutta tutkimusta ja lähteetöntä' ('rv, original research and unsourced'). Level 3: only one signal (sources); one anonymous range (91.155.x.x), one article, put back only once, so it stays at level 2. Candidates c11 and c05; c04 is the re-insertion seen from the other side.

items.why: Level 2. Claim: 'Suomen historiaa on vääristelty ja yritetty tuhota valloittajien toimesta satoja vuosia' ('Finland's history has been distorted, and conquerors have worked to destroy it, for hundreds of years'), 'Ruotsin vallan aikan oli säädetty jopa kuolemantuomio sille joka kertoisi suomen historiasta' ('under Swedish rule a death sentence was even decreed for anyone who told Finland's history'), and a numbered list 'SUOMEN KUNINKAAT ENNEN RUOTSALAISIA' ('kings of Finland before the Swedes'). Community dispute: removed by another account after 8.4 h with 'huuhaat pois' ('out with the hokum'), a judgement on the accuracy of the content. Not graffiti: coherent prose with a numbered source list. One editor, one article, never put back, so level 2. Candidate c12.

items.description: Adds a 'genetic research' section saying genetic studies point to Finno-Ugric roots of historical rulers and that Rurik belonged to the Finno-Ugric haplogroup N.
items.why: Level 2. Claim: 'Käynnissä olevien geenitutkimuksen projektien tuloksista on jo nyt löytynyt viitteitä historiallisten hallitsijoiden suomalais-ugrilaisista juurista' ('results of ongoing genetic research projects already show indications of Finno-Ugric roots of historical rulers') and 'Tähän mennessä on selvinnyt, että Rurik ei ollut haploryhmältään viikinkeihin kuuluvaa I-ryhmää eikä slaavilaista ryhmää, vaan suomalais-ugrilaista N-haploryhmää' ('it has so far turned out that Rurik was not in the Viking haplogroup I or a Slavic group but in the Finno-Ugric haplogroup N'), in an article on ancient Finnish kings. Community dispute: removed after 2.8 days by another account with 'poistettu asiaanliittymätön (suomalaisugrilainen != suomalainen), ja todennäköisesti täysi hömppä - Rurik tai ainakin suvut ovat fiktiivisiä' ('removed as irrelevant (Finno-Ugric != Finnish), and probably complete nonsense; Rurik or at least the lineages are fictional'): about accuracy. The flags also show this removal was undone by rev 3625211 (not in the pack, so not listed); the text is not in the latest revision. One editor (both edits by E385), one article, so level 2. Candidate c09.

items.label: contested
items.description: Adds that a 1930s encyclopedia concluded the Sámi learned their Finno-Ugric language from the Finns and that current DNA research does not support a separate origin of Sámi and Finns.

items.label: campaign
items.description: Adds that SKE's chair Marco de Wit has been convicted of an aggravated accounting offence and aggravated endangerment of traffic safety; the de Wit version also adds suspicions of two further offences for which it says he was acquitted.
items.why: Level 3. Level 2 holds: a slanted claim about a living person. The de Wit version reads 'De Wit on tuomittu vankeuteen törkeästä kirjanpitorikoksesta ... sakkorangaistuksiin kahdesta törkeästä liikenneturvallisuuden vaarantamisesta' ('sentenced to prison for an aggravated accounting offence ... fined for two aggravated endangerments of traffic safety'), plus suspicions of two serious offences 'mutta näytön puuttuessa oikeus on todennut hänet syyttömäksi' ('but for lack of evidence the court found him not guilty'), tagged {{lähde}}. It was removed with 'Mahdollinen kunnianloukkaus. Ei voi lisätä lähteettömänä.' ('Possible defamation. Cannot be added without a source.', 17769625, c17) and 'Rikoksia ei voi lisätä lähteettöminä. Muilta osin POV.' ('Crimes cannot be added unsourced. Otherwise POV.', 17769831, c02). It was put back twice on 2018-12-11: 17769622 undoes an earlier removal 17769615 that is not in the pack, then 17769627. Level-3 signals: (1) articles: the same two convictions were added to Suomen Kansa Ensin on 2018-11-04 (17685226: 'Yhdistyksen puheenjohtaja on tuomittu rangaistuksiin muun muassa törkeästä kirjanpitorikosesta ja törkeästä liikenneturvallisuuden vaarantamisesta' = 'the association's chair has been sentenced for, among other things, an aggravated accounting offence and aggravated endangerment of traffic safety'; removed by a rollback 5.8 h later, c15) and to Marco de Wit. (2) accounts: two anonymous editors in different masked ranges (E539 88.115.x.x on SKE, E555 83.245.x.x on de Wit). (3) persistence: put back 2 times, 37 days between the first insertion (2018-11-04) and the last (2018-12-11). Treating the two articles as one claim is a judgement: the wording differs but the two convictions are the same. Without that merge, the de Wit part alone is level 2 (one editor, one article).

items.why: Level 2. A claim: loaded framing in the added text ('alatyylisen [[Kansallismielisyys|kansallismielisen]] blogin' = 'vulgar nationalist blog'; 'De Wit tuli tunnetuksi kuljetettuaan ruumita pakettiauton lattialla' = 'De Wit became known for transporting corpses on the floor of a van'). Community dispute: the run was removed after 107 min by a different account with 'Muilta osin POV' ('otherwise POV', 17769831, c02). Not level 3: there are two editors in different masked ranges (E555 83.245.x.x; E619 185.77.x.x changed 'verkkojulkaisun' to 'blogin', 'web publication' to 'blog', the same framing), but only one article, no put-back and no source change, so only one signal. Contains must-include rev 17769637, which adds 'alatyylisen' ('vulgar'). The convictions paragraph that was re-added in the same run is item far-right/i01.

items.description: Rewrites the IKL lead as a 'far-right fascist party that took many influences from German National Socialism and European fascism' and says its black-shirt uniform had a swastika armband 'like the Nazis'.
items.why: Level 2. A claim: it changes how IKL is characterised. Rendered added text: 'äärioikeistolainen fasistipuolue, joka otti runsaasti vaikutteita saksalaisesta kansallissosialistisesta ja eurooppalaisesta fasistisesta liikkeestä' ('a far-right fascist party that took many influences from the German National Socialist and European fascist movement'); 'joissa oli natsien lailla hakaristihihamerkki' ('which, like the Nazis, had a swastika armband'). Community dispute: it was removed without a summary on 2007-04-12 (2659257, c05), put back by E15 (2659601, c18) and removed again 15 min later (2659647). That is one put-back and a back-and-forth (6 identity reverts in 3 days). Not level 3: two editors added parts of it (E15, named; E117, 213.216.x.x), but it is on one article, was put back only once and has no source change, so only one signal. items.description: Replaces the SKE board in the infobox with the rival board elected in 2019 and adds a signed note that the PRH removed de Wit's signing rights; later adds that the Tampere district court backed the new board (YouTube source).
items.why: Level 2. A claim that changes who leads the party during a leadership split. The infobox chair becomes the rival board's chair, and the added note reads '23.8.PRH poisti Marcolta nimenkirjoitusoikeudet. Hän ei ole enää puolueen puheenjohtaja, ei edes hallituksen jäsen.' ('On 23 Aug the PRH removed Marco's signing rights. He is no longer the party chair, not even a board member.'). Community dispute, step by step: (1) removed as 'lähteetön' ('unsourced', 18391755, c19); (2) put back the same day by another named account with 'Luotettavin käytettävissä oleva julkinen tieto on PRH:n rekisteri' ('the most reliable public information is the PRH register', 18392074); (3) that account then removed the signed note as wrong: 'PRH ei voi poistaa keneltäkään mitään oikeuksia' ('the PRH cannot remove anyone's rights', 18392075, c20); (4) after 61 days the whole change was removed again: 'ei minkäänlaisia luotettavia sekundäärilähteitä. joku muutaman sadan tilaajan youtube-kanava ei ole luotettava lähde' ('no reliable secondary sources at all; a YouTube channel with a few hundred subscribers is not a reliable source', 18519639, c07). Not level 3: three named accounts added or re-added it (E592, E540, E594), but it is on one article and was put back only once. The citation swaps visible in c07 (party site and rules reference changed to a new domain) cannot be tied to an edit in the pack, so the source signal is not counted. Other editors' edits in the run (18396968, a 'fix', a homepage-link update) are left out.

A claim with narrative framing: 'Lapuan liikkeen ruotsinkielisestä kannattajakunnasta on aikojen saatossa enemmän tai vähemmän vaiettu' ('the movement's Swedish-speaking support has over time been more or less hushed up'), and 'Ironista kylläkin ... väheksyivät suomen kieltä' ('Ironically ... belittled the Finnish language'). Community dispute, two signals: a {{lähde}} (citation needed) tag was added to it during its 122.6 days; and the removal gives a sourcing and accuracy reason, 'poistan pitkään lähteettömänä olleen kappaleen ... Aiemman kappaleen lähteen mukaan kannattajakuntaa ei ole juuri tutkittu, eikä siinä puhuta sanaakaan ruotsinkielisistä' ('removing the long-unsourced paragraph ... according to the previous paragraph's source the support base has hardly been studied, and it says not a word about Swedish speakers', c37). The text-search inserting edit 1420030 does add this paragraph (insertion_diff). One editor, one article, not put back: not level 3.

items.description: Changes the SKE infobox title of its secretary from 'party secretary' to 'secretary', on the grounds that SKE was not yet a registered party.

A claim: a content dispute over SKE's status that can be quoted from the added text ('(sihteeri)' instead of '(puoluesihteeri)'; summary 'Ei voi olla puoluesihteeri, koska ei ole puolue!' = 'Cannot be a party secretary because it is not a party!'). So: put back once, in a back-and-forth. Not level 3: two masked ranges (E543 23.233.x.x, E539 88.115.x.x), but one article and one put-back give only one signal. The change is only 6 bytes, so a reviewer may prefer level 1.

('Wikipedia is not for promoting your own blog. Your source is not reliable.') and 'Lähde ei täytä luotettavan lähteen määritelmää' ('the source does not meet the definition of a reliable source'). A reviewer who reads this inclusion war as a content dispute would get level 2, and E240's single re-add plus persistence would then even meet two level-3 signals. Two inserting accounts (anonymous 87.95.x.x and a named restorer), but one article, one put-back and no source manipulation: one level-3 signal only. Other edits in the c05 run are item i05 or dropped (a link, a deletion tag undone within the run).

items.description: Puts back a passage saying 'Kalevala culture' is mentioned in the Anglo-Saxon poem Widsith ('Ja Caelic hallitsi finnejä', 'And Caelic ruled the Finns'), with a list of scholars who linked Caelic to Kaleva.
items.why: Level 2. Claim, quoted from the added text: 'Kalevalainen kulttuuri tarkoittaa suomalaisten tai suomensukuisten väestöjen mytologiaa, josta on maininta anglosaksisessa muinaisrunossa WIDSITH, joka on muistiinmerkitty 600 -luvulta' ('Kalevala culture means the mythology of the Finns or Finnic peoples, which is mentioned in the Anglo-Saxon ancient poem WIDSITH, written down in the 600s'): it states a scholarly identification (Caelic = Kaleva) as a mention of 'Kalevala culture'. Community dispute: removed by a different account (E23) after 15 min with the summary 'poisto, Widsithin spekulatiivinen yhteys Kalevaan mainintaan jo' ('removal, Widsith's speculative connection to Kaleva [is] already mentioned'), which calls the connection speculative (accuracy) besides duplicate; and the inserting summary begins 'PALAUTETTU' ('RESTORED'), so this edit itself put the text back after an earlier removal that the pack does not show. Not level 3: one account (E30, named), one article; only one insertion is visible, so persistence cannot be shown. Not kept (removal not undone). Weakest point: the removal summary's main reason is duplication. Candidate c09.

items.description: Adds to 'Kalevalan synty' that epic poetry is found almost everywhere, has often been compiled into written epics, and that the Kalevala would hardly have come about without the model of earlier epics (cited to SKS).
items.why: Level 2. Claim (content dispute over the Kalevala's origin), quoted from the added text: 'Kalevalakaan tuskin olisi syntynyt ilman edeltäneiden eepposten mallia' ('the Kalevala, too, would hardly have come about without the model of earlier epics'). Community dispute: an edit war over this passage on 2007-01-03 from 10:31 UTC until just after 11:12. E30 removed its opening sentence (2138187, summary 'Väärää tietoa, turhana pois, koska eeppistä runoutta ei ole kirjoitettuna kuin Kreikassa, Suomessa ja Virossa', 'Wrong information, removed as unnecessary, because epic poetry exists in written form only in Greece, Finland and Estonia'); E23 restored it 76 s later (2138193, c29), which 2138201 undid; E23 then added the longer passage (2138403, c12, summary: the worldwide perspective is essential and its absence is one of the article's worst gaps); E30 removed it after 5 min (2138429, summary: the culture behind the Kalevala did not read other countries' epics); E31 put it back (2138438, c17); E30 removed it again 73 s later (2138447), and that removal was undone by 2138450. So: an accuracy summary ('Väärää tietoa'), put back 4 times, a back-and-forth. Inserting revs here are the two pack edits that added the passage (2138193 and 2138450 appear only as removal-undo ids). Not level 3: two inserting accounts (E23, E31) is one signal, but one article, all re-insertions within about 45 min, no source change. Review caveat: not kept by the flag (the 2007 wording is not in the latest revision), but the same passage, reworded, is still in the 2008 version restored in c25 and survives the 2017 rewrite in c30; if the latest revision still has it, 'kept' would apply instead.
